Below it the grey-beige rock face runs about rows 18-28, with a dark base shadow at rows 28-29. The snow ends on a darker line at rows 18-20, which acts as the front edge. At least 11 rows of front face sit under the top, so it is a 3/4 view and not a flat slab or a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small snow-covered rock, not a tree, bush or plant with a canopy and trunk, so it does not match the reference kind. It is far smaller than the tree references and sits in less than one tile of area, so the per-tile density fact is only a rough guide. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which means the outline is a neutral dark grey/black line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material, as in the references (0%). A careful artist would find it flatter and more sticker-like next to the tree references.
